text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Friday.

GERMANY - DTB Bund futures gain remained in softer ground after U.S. Q1 GDP was revised up to 5.8 pct from 5.6 pct. Analysts had expected an upward revision. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.77, up 0.29 from Wednesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts closed at their highs on Friday, boosted by a U.S. Treasuries rally. But they faced a big week ahead with the budget date to be announced, the new monetary committee meeting and key U.S. jobs data due. The June gilt future settled 14/32 higher at 112-20. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 112-21/32, up 15/32 from Thursday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond and interest rate futures climbed ahead of the final round of a parliamentary election as investors bought back contracts they had sold earlier, to reduce their exposure in case of post-poll rally, trader said. The June notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.52 up 0.38 from Thursday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian debt markets rebounded from the day's lows by the close after a day marked by rumours and flood of economic information. The government's three-year economic plan disappointed some traders who said it failed to address structural reforms. Others said it was in line with expectations. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 128.99 up 0.27 from Thursday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - US Treasuries moved slightly higher after NY Fed President McDonough said 2nd quarter GDP data pointed to a slowing economy. Chicago PMI report mixed, prices up while employment down. Equity weakness in Europe seen helping to support market. Market focus shifts to NAPM, nonfarm payrolls next week. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 109-26/32, up 16/32 from Thursday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.94 percent.

JAPAN - Key June 10-year Japanese goverment bonds (JGB) futures ended sharply higher, but pared some earlier gains in the afternoon after LDP official said he saw a chance of a credit tightening by early autumn. But overall sentiment strong, as expectations of an imminent credit tightening eased after Thursday's output data.In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 124.00, up 0.15 from Thursday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The primary market saw little fresh supply ahead of the weekend, save some activity in Austrian schillings and guilders. Argentina is expected to launch a 10-year bond of up to 200 million pounds via HSBC and UBS next week. Brazil could also launch its first Eurolire bond next week. Brazil's dollar global bond may also be launched next week as part of a swap or buy back of Brady bonds. Romania is expected to launch its first mark-denominated bond.
